To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of automated variables, especially laboratory and comorbity variables, improves the accuracy of length of stay prediction; (2) the use of these variables is particularly beneficial for patients in intensive care and in the emergency department, for whom the length of stay is more difficult to predict; and (3) the use of laboratory and comorbility variables is more important in hospitals that have a higher percentage of intensive care patients.
the use of automated comorbidity and laboratory variables improves the prediction of length of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU) and that this improvement is clinically relevant.
